x-d@L,?hu^Q;7{0v9pD3.text:
Writes a single line of text to the canvas.

Inputs:
- Pos: The (x, y) position of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The x-position of the text. (must be a number)
    2. The y-position of the text. (must be a number)
    - Default value: (0.0, 0.0)
- Size: The size and width of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The size of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Equal to the height of the letter H, in pixels.
    2. The width of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Multiplies by the size to affect the width of characters.
    - Default value: (12.0, 1.0)
- Bounds: Limits where text may be rendered.
  - Values:
    1. The minimum x-position where a character can be drawn. (must be a number)
    2. The maximum x-position where a character can be drawn. (must be a number)
    - Default value: (-Infinity, Infinity)
  - Note: characters may extend slightly beyond each bound.
- Space: The spacing between each character.
  - Values:
    - Any number
      - Adds (0.27 * (character spacing) * (size)) number of pixels between each character.
    - Default value: 1.0
- Style: The style of the text
  - Values:
    1. The weight of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Sets the pen size to (0.125 * (weight) * (size))
    2. The slant of the text, in degrees. (must be a number n such that -90.0 < n < 90.0)
      - A positive value results in a forward slant, a negative value results in a backward slant.
    - Default value: (1.0, 0.0)
- Underline: Controls the underline.
  - Values:
    1. The vertical position of the underline (must be a number)
      - Negative values result in an underline. (-0.25 is recommended)
      - Values between 0.0 and 1.0 result in a strikethrough. (0.4 is recommended)
      - Values above 1.0 result in an overline.
    2. The weight of the underline (must be a number)
      - Height of the underline = (0.1 * (underline weight) * (size))
    - Default value: no underline; weight defaults to 0.1 when the first input contains a value
- Align: The alignment of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The horizontal alignment of the text. Can be a number or one of the following letters:
      - L / l: left alignment (equivalent to 0.0)
      - C / c: centered alignment (equivalent to 0.5)
      - R / r: right alignment (equivalent to 1.0)
    2. The vertical alignment of the text. Can be a number or one of the following letters:
      - B / b: bottom alignment (equivalent to 0.0)
      - C / c: centered alignment (equivalent to 0.5)
      - T / t: top alignment (equivalent to 1.0)
    - Default value: (L, B)
- Text: The text to be written.
  - Values:
    - Any data type that can be converted to a string
    - Default value: none

pd!:rU@rkhf/FL0dx`~].text: In order to use Pen Text Engine++ in a project, drag the TextEngine sprite to your backpack and drag the backpacked sprite into the project. Credit would be greatly appreciated, and the manner in which it is given is up to your best judgment.

lP|~1dP}a1mIc=ZfMnWH.text:
Custom blocks that have an underscore ('_') at the beginning of their names are used internally by the text engine. Do not touch them unless you know what you are doing.

Lists that have an underscore ('_') at the beginning of their names contain data that the text engine uses to render text. Altering some of these lists could seriously affect the text engine's ability to render text.

If you want to view the names of the available fonts, look at the _fontName list.

.V1f~2,(Ka!pDGEtnuFD.text:
Many of the inputs in the custom blocks can be left blank, using a default value instead. Some features are disabled if their inputs are left blank, making Pen Text Engine++ easier  and quicker to use.

If a value of a possible input is surrounded by quotes, don't include the quotes when using that input. The quotes merely indicate that a possible input is a string.

Writes multiple lines of text to the canvas.

Inputs:
- Pos: The (x, y) position of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The x-position of the start of the first line. (must be a number)
      - When left blank, the first line will respect the horizontal alignment between the x-bounds.
    2. The y-position of the text. (must be a number)
    - Default value: (none, 0.0)
- Size: The size and width of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The size of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Equal to the height of the letter H, in pixels.
    2. The width of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Multiplies by the size to affect the width of characters.
    - Default value: (12.0, 1.0)
- Bounds: Limits where text may be rendered.
  - Values:
    1. The minimum x-position of each line, affecting wrapping. (must be a number)
    2. The maximum x-position of each line, affecting wrapping. (must be a number)
    3. The maximum y-position where a line can be drawn. (must be a number)
    4. The minimum y-position where a line can be drawn. (must be a number)
    - Default value: (-230.0, 230.0, Infinity, -Infinity)
  - Note: characters may extend slightly beyond each bound.
- Space: The spacing between each character.
  - Values:
    1. The spacing between each character. (must be a number)
      - Adds (0.27 * (character spacing) * (size)) number of pixels between each character.
    2. The spacing between each line. (must be a number)
      - Adds (0.7 * (line spacing) * (size)) number of pixels between each line.
    - Default value: (1.0, 1.0)
- Style: The style of the text
  - Values:
    1. The weight of the text. (must be a positive number)
      - Sets the pen size to (0.125 * (weight) * (size))
    2. The slant of the text, in degrees. (must be a number n such that -90.0 < n < 90.0)
      - A positive value results in a forward slant, a negative value results in a backward slant.
    - Default value: (1.0, 0.0)
- Underline: Controls the underline.
  - Values:
    1. The vertical position of the underline (must be a number)
      - Negative values result in an underline (-0.25 is recommended)
      - Values between 0.0 and 1.0 result in a strikethrough (0.4 is recommended)
      - Values above 1.0 result in an overline
    2. The weight of the underline (must be a number)
      - Height of the underline = (0.1 * (underline weight) * (size))
    - Default value: no underline; weight defaults to 0.1 when the first input contains a value
- Align: The alignment of the text.
  - Values:
    1. The horizontal alignment of the text. Can be a number or one of the following letters:
      - L / l: left alignment (equivalent to 0.0)
      - C / c: centered alignment (equivalent to 0.5)
      - R / r: right alignment (equivalent to 1.0)
    2. The vertical alignment of the text. Can be a number or one of the following letters:
      - Any number: the y-position of the text represents the bottom of the nth line.
      - T / t: the y-position of the text represents the top of the first line of text.
      - C / c: the y-position of the text represents the vertical midpoint of the lines of text.
      - B / b: the y-position of the text represents the bottom of the last line of text.
    - Default value: (L, 1.0)
- Text: The text to be written.
  - Values:
    - Any data type that can be converted to a string
    - Default value: none

@!TvNt[QMtU1LO=G@bjA.text:
INJECTING FONTS

If you want to add new fonts to Pen Text Engine++, use the font injector at https://RexScratch.github.io/PenTextEngineInjector/. To use the font injector, you will need to download your project first.

The font injector includes the option to remove all font data from a TextEngine sprite. There is also the option to remove list monitor data, which slightly reduces the file size (you shouldn't have to worry about file size unless you are using a large number of fonts).
